```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# Show stores below the temporary folder as `<tempdir>/...` and use UTC, so
# that the output is the same on every machine.
local({
  dirs <- unique(c(
    normalizePath(tempdir(), winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE),
    normalizePath(tempdir(), winslash = "\\", mustWork = FALSE),
    tempdir()
  ))
  hide <- function(x) {
    for (d in dirs) x <- gsub(d, "<tempdir>", x, fixed = TRUE)
    x
  }
  for (h in c("output", "message", "warning", "error")) {
    old <- knitr::knit_hooks$get(h)
    knitr::knit_hooks$set(stats::setNames(
      list(local({
        old <- old
        function(x, options) old(hide(x), options)
      })),
      h
    ))
  }
})
old_options <- options(width = 80, cli.width = 120, cli.hyperlink = FALSE)
old_tz <- Sys.getenv("TZ", unset = NA)
Sys.setenv(TZ = "UTC")
```

# rcs

rcs (R Cloud Storage) keeps tabular data, geospatial vector data (`sf`) and
rasters (`terra`) from R in one *store*, mostly as Parquet files. A store is
kept in one *primary* location and any number of *secondary* ones: local
folders or Google Cloud Storage buckets.

- **Catalog first.** Each location holds a small catalog of its datasets
  and files. Every function starts from it: listing a store, describing a
  dataset or finding the files a filter needs reads no data file.
- **Every write lands everywhere, verified.** A write goes to the primary
  and to every secondary, each file is checked by its MD5 checksum, and the
  catalog is switched last, so readers see the old or the new version,
  never a mixture.
- **Reads fetch only what they need.** Filters and column selections are
  passed to the Parquet reader. Spatial filters use H3 cells and bounding
  boxes stored with the data, so an area is read without scanning every
  geometry.
- **Lazy first.** `store_open()` opens a dataset without reading it; dplyr
  verbs describe the rows you want, and `collect()` reads them into R.
- **DuckDB in one call.** `store_duckdb()` turns every dataset into a
  DuckDB view, in memory or in a database file next to your own tables,
  and `store_write()` stores a DuckDB result without loading it into R.
- **Same data, same version.** Writing identical data again changes
  nothing and copies nothing.

## Installation

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("EBukin/rcs")
```

Geospatial datasets need the package h3o, rasters need terra, DuckDB
needs duckdb, DBI and dbplyr, and Google Cloud Storage needs gargle and
httr2 and an arrow build with GCS support.

## Example

Create a store in a folder, here a temporary one, and write a table. The
data are simulated by `rcs_sim_table()`.

```{r}
library(rcs)

st <- store_connect(file.path(tempdir(), "my-store"), create = TRUE)

store_write(st, rcs_sim_table(500, seed = 1), "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales",
  description = "Simulated daily sales by shop and product.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"),
  partition = "year"
)
```

See what the store holds:

```{r}
st
```

Open a dataset. Nothing is read yet; printing shows a header and the
first rows.

```{r}
q <- store_open(st, "sales/daily")
q
```

Describe the rows you want with dplyr verbs and read them with
`collect()`. Only the file of the year 2024 is opened.

```{r}
q |>
  dplyr::filter(year == 2024, qty > 45) |>
  dplyr::select(shop_id, date, product, qty) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

`store_read(st, "sales/daily", year == 2024, qty > 45)` does the same in
one call.

Query the whole store with SQL in DuckDB, without copying any data:

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("duckdb", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("DBI", quietly = TRUE)}
con <- store_duckdb(st)
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT year, sum(qty) AS qty FROM sales.daily GROUP BY year ORDER BY year")
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```

Keep the same store in a bucket and in a local copy; writes reach both and
reads use the local copy:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
st <- store_connect("gs://my-bucket/store", secondary = "~/data/my-store")
```

## Learn more

- `vignette("rcs")`: getting started with a local store: write, open,
  read, update, keep versions.
- `vignette("duckdb")`: datasets as DuckDB views, database files, spatial
  filters in DuckDB, writing from DuckDB, the local-first workflow.
- `vignette("locations")`: primary and secondary locations, environment
  variables, cloud credentials, sync.
- `vignette("geospatial")`: `sf` objects, spatial filters, geocoding
  engines, rasters.

The package is developed and tested on simulated data only.

```{r, include = FALSE}
unlink(file.path(tempdir(), "my-store"), recursive = TRUE)
options(old_options)
if (is.na(old_tz)) Sys.unsetenv("TZ") else Sys.setenv(TZ = old_tz)
```
